scope: High-confidence recent projects discovered through public Reddit/X/GitHub search and verified against each project's primary repository or maintainer page. Includes game and software targets; social posts are discovery references, never the only evidence when a repository exists. All media URLs are remote HTTPS URIs; no assets are copied into the repository.

projects.title: Super Metroid C# Port
projects.platform: SNES Japan/USA NTSC v1.0 ROM → Windows x64 and Android ARM64
projects.status: The project README describes the C# port as playable from the opening through the ending, with minor known glitches. Windows x64 and Android ARM64 release builds are listed; users must provide a supported NTSC v1.0 ROM.
projects.summary: Translates the original Super Metroid program into readable, commented C#. The ROM supplies graphics, room data, tables and audio resources; the shared managed game core uses a Direct3D 11 renderer with software fallback on Windows and a software renderer on Android. This is a behavior-preserving C# port, not a byte-matching recompilation. It is distinct from the cataloged SNES recompilation and annotated disassembly projects.
projects.strategy: Behavioral translation of the original game program into a managed C# implementation; the user's supported ROM supplies game data and serves as the reference.
projects.source_available: Public C# source and Windows/Android releases. The user must provide a Japan/USA NTSC v1.0 ROM; ROMs and extracted game assets are not included.
projects.subtype: C# native port from translated game program

projects.status: Active matching decompilation. The README's 2026-10-16 snapshot reports 6,378/7,223 functions in C (88.3%) and 49.6% of .text bytes; the build is reported to match the original ELF byte-for-byte.

The project documents the exact supported disc and boot ELF hashes. It also has a separate future mod build and English-translation roadmap; neither is represented here as a released translation or port. The repository does not include game data, and setup starts from the user's own disc image.
projects.strategy: Matching source reconstruction using the original Sony Emotion Engine compiler family and byte-for-byte executable comparison.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; the user supplies the Japanese PS2 disc image. Game code and disc data are not included.

projects.title: HyperBlade Windows Matching Decompilation
projects.status: Active matching decompilation. The README reports 2,791/3,054 game functions matching exactly, covering 75.34% of game-code bytes. A basic Windows bring-up shim runs the game in a simplest-form test build; the project directs modern-system play to a separate port.
projects.summary: Rebuilds HyperBlade's 1996 Windows executable from source with Visual C++ 6.0 SP3 and scores functions using reccmp. Only the patched v1.0.0.1 executable matches the documented reference. The repository contains source and a basic bring-up build, not the game binary or data; the player must provide a copy.
projects.strategy: Matching decompilation measured against the original executable and compiler; the separately maintained hyperblade-20XX project is the modern portable port.
projects.source_available: Public source; the user supplies the original patched HYPERX.EXE v1.0.0.1 and game data. No game binary is included.

projects.title: Zombie Revenge Dreamcast Decompilation
projects.status: Kick-off stage, active. The README reports 1,026/4,232 functions named. The build reconstructs the executable byte-for-byte, while C functions are tracked separately for equivalent behavior; matching C is described as a later/bonus tier.
projects.summary: A Dreamcast decompilation whose setup extracts the user's original 1ST_READ.BIN, generates one assembly unit per function and verifies rebuilt bytes. The README identifies the supported European retail build and its hash, and explicitly states the repository contains no game code or data. projects.source_available: Public source; the user supplies a matching European Dreamcast disc and a Katana SDK. Game code/data are generated locally and ignored by Git.

projects.title: Lezac DOS Software Decompilation and REA Study
projects.game: Larax & Zaco LEZAC.EXE v1.0 shareware software
projects.platform: 16-bit DOS x86 software (LEZAC.EXE v1.0); native differential probes and DOSBox-X reference
projects.status: Active evidence-backed reverse engineering. The README reports 215 procedures exported, seven routines reconstructed in original-style Pascal and six portable C routines, plus differential tests against the original executable. It explicitly says this is not a playable or bit-identical rebuild and not recovered original source.
projects.summary: Reverse-engineers the LEZAC shareware executable with REA and Ghidra. Public artifacts include evidence-linked function dossiers, pseudocode and assembly listings, recovered Pascal/C routines, packed-layout measurements, and native-versus-original probes. The author carefully distinguishes these reconstructions from original source recovery and a complete playable rebuild.
projects.strategy: Evidence-backed software reverse engineering, with selected routines reconstructed and differentially tested; full matching or a playable rebuild is not claimed.
projects.source_available: Public analysis, tests and reconstruction source; README identifies the original LEZAC.EXE as an external reference and does not claim to include the original executable or source.
projects.subtype: DOS application reverse engineering and partial routine reconstruction

projects.source_available: Public tooling, reconstructed source and research; original Roblox client files are not committed or shared and must remain user-supplied.

projects.title: Petari for Apple Silicon: Super Mario Galaxy Native macOS Port
projects.game: Super Mario Galaxy (USA Wii RMGE01 revision 0)
projects.platform: Wii USA RMGE01 revision 0 → macOS on Apple Silicon ARM64 (Metal via Aurora); developed on macOS 27
projects.status: The maintainer describes the game as playable in a development build. Automated tests enter all 135 galaxy missions and check movement, jump, spin, camera and pause; not every mission has been completed and the ending is unplayed. Physical controllers are untested and visual fidelity is not yet systematically compared.
projects.summary: An independent native Apple Silicon port based on the Petari Super Mario Galaxy decompilation. It compiles the original game code for ARM64 and renders through Metal using Aurora rather than an emulator. The port adds native menus and optional gameplay helpers; users must supply/extract their own USA revision-0 disc data. The repository is explicit that this native-port work is not decompilation work and is not intended for upstream Petari.
projects.strategy: Native ARM64 compilation of Petari's reconstructed game code with a Metal renderer through Aurora; game-specific native port changes are maintained separately.
projects.source_available: Public port source, licensed CC0-1.0. The user supplies the USA RMGE01 revision-0 disc data; the repository contains no Nintendo game assets.

projects.title: OpenPopTB-MacOS: Populous: The Beginning Native Recompilation
projects.game: Populous: The Beginning (1998) and Undiscovered Worlds expansion
projects.platform: Original Windows x86 executables → Apple Silicon macOS ARM64; signed release requires macOS 14+, source build supports macOS 12+
projects.status: The maintainer reports single-player fully playable through the campaign, tutorial, Rolling Demo and Undiscovered Worlds expansion, with original software-rendered graphics, sound, music and FMV audio. Multiplayer remains unfinished. GitHub release v0.1.2 is listed as a signed/notarized Apple Silicon build.
projects.summary: Statically recompiles the original Windows x86 executables and QMixer sound DLL into C and runs them on a small Win32/DirectDraw/DirectInput/DirectSound compatibility runtime over SDL3. The user supplies a GOG or compatible Windows game installation; the first launch recompiles it locally. The project is distinct from the cataloged general-purpose Recomp-Kit static recompiler: this repository provides a game-specific, playable Populous port, and contains no game code or data.
projects.strategy: Static x86-to-C recompilation plus a game-specific Win32/DirectX API runtime implemented over SDL3; no emulator, Wine or VM is used.
projects.source_available: Public recompiler and runtime, plus signed/notarized releases. The user must own and supply the GOG or compatible game copy; no game code or data are included.
projects.subtype: Windows x86 static recompilation to native Apple Silicon
